inputs.base_revenue_note: TTM UNDERLYING revenue to 30 June 2026 = FY2025 20,080 + H1 FY2026 11,279 - H1 FY2025 9,057. Underlying (hedge-rate) revenue is the basis of guidance and margins; statutory FY2025 was 21,207 (spot-rate translation).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 June 2026: 8,355m in issue (called-up share capital GBP1,671m / 20p) less 1.4m treasury shares and ~60m shares held by the Employee Benefit Trust (69.3m at Dec-25, treated as cancelled in the EPS table) plus 18m dilutive options (H1 FY2026 EPS note). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the GBP7-9bn 2026-28 buyback is value-neutral in this model and GBP293m settled after 30 June is not reflected.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash flow statement 'Share-based payments' add-back: FY2025 104 (RR.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:9281), H1 FY2026 43, H1 FY2025 60; TTM 87. No net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes 0). SBC-light market: 0.4% of revenue.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM financing outflow to 30 June 2026: FY2025 1,008 + H1 FY2026 1,097 - H1 FY2025 380 = 1,725 (cash paid, not authorisation). Repurchaser: the flat count is funded. GBP2.5bn planned for 2026 within the GBP7-9bn 2026-28 programme.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quoted pence. No cross-listing parity needed; US ADR (RYCEY) is OTC 1:1 and not used.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP flows discounted at a GBP-built rate: UK 10y gilt ~4.5% + beta ~1.0 x ERP 4.5% = 9.0% cost of equity; net cash so WACC = cost of equity, 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios - cyclicality, durability and LTSA-unwind risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights. The market price implies a materially lower required return (see required_return_table).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full lease cash payment (capital element 232 + interest element 74 in FY2025 financing; TTM ~352 = 1.5% of underlying revenue) charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (GBP1,656m at 30 June 2026) EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is borrowings 2,651 (4 current + 2,647 non-current) plus 37 fair value of hedging swaps. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (TTM underlying ex-ROU ~680 = 3.0%).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI equity GBP27m at FY2025 - immaterial, no adjustment. Rolls-Royce SMR was deconsolidated 4 March 2025 (55.3% equity-accounted associate); its small share of losses stays in the flows and the stake is added in the equity bridge at carrying value.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2, non-US cyclical industrial, adaptations read: currency, leases, NCI, matching-asset rule). FLOW BASE: TTM to 30 June 2026, not FY2025, so the 30 June balance sheet and the flows line up and H1 2026 cash generation is not counted twice. reported_fcf = OCF - capex (FY2025 3,580 + H1 FY2026 2,180 - H1 FY2025 1,649 = 4,111); interest paid and lease payments sit in financing so OCF is pre-interest. last_fcf = 4,111 - 87 SBC - 230 interest income = 3,794; the lease cash (~352) is additionally charged in the forward build, giving a TTM owner FCF ex-lease of ~3,440 (15.4% of underlying revenue) against the company's own TTM 'free cash flow' of ~3,650 (which excludes GBP148m/yr of excess-derivative settlements that this model keeps in the flows). PEAK-EARNINGS GUARD: the base case takes FY2026 guidance (GBP4.7-4.9bn underlying operating profit, GBP3.8-4.0bn FCF) as the year-1 run-rate and then holds EBITDA margin flat at ~25% (operating margin ~20.5%) rather than extrapolating the H1 FY2026 22.5% margin, which management attributes partly to LTSA contract catch-ups. Statutory FY2025 net income (5,841) and EPS (69.4p) are ignored: they carry the GBP809m SMR deconsolidation gain and GBP1,658m of derivative fair-value financing income. Historical CAGRs are trough-to-recovery (FY2020-22 were COVID losses with negative equity) and are not used to set growth; the base path is anchored to guidance and the 2028 mid-term targets. Interest income stripped because net cash (3.8bn) exceeds the FCF base. Cash in the bridge is the full GBP6,484m; a portion supports GBP17bn of LTSA contract liabilities, so the bridge is generous by perhaps GBP1-2bn (12-24p/share).

equity_bridge.item: Rolls-Royce SMR Ltd 55.3% equity-accounted stake at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: Recognised at fair value GBP732m on deconsolidation 4 March 2025 (validated by CEZ Group's cash investment) plus GBP52m 2025 additions (RR.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:11934-11942). Its share of losses remains in the flows (conservative). Other JV/associate stakes (HAESL, SAESL etc., ~GBP470m) are NOT added because their dividends (GBP88m FY2025) are inside OCF.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case years 1-5 average (guidance-anchored); historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward proxy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity and EPS CAGRs are undefined: shareholders' equity was negative FY2019-FY2024 (-3,376 to -912) and turned positive only in FY2025 (2,726); statutory EPS was negative in FY2019-FY2022. Revenue 5-yr CAGR of 13.0% starts at the FY2020 COVID trough (11,491) - from pre-COVID FY2019 (16,587) the 6-year CAGR is 4.2%. Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR of 56% (845 -> 3,206, SBC and interest income stripped) is a recovery from a distressed base, not a trend; it is marginally below the reported-FCF CAGR (56.8%) because interest income on the rebuilt cash pile grew faster than FCF.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series used for the FCF CAGR: FY2022 928-47-36 = 845; FY2025 3,580-104-270 = 3,206. FY2020 owner FCF -3,995 and FY2021 -854 make the 5-yr figure undefined.

base.narrative: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) = FY2026 guidance run-rate plus half a year of growth: 11% revenue growth, 25.0% EBITDA margin which after 0.5% SBC, 1.5% lease cash and 3.0% ex-ROU D&A gives ~20% operating margin (FY2026 guidance GBP4.7-4.9bn on ~GBP23.7bn). Growth then decelerates 8/7/6/5% as the widebody OE delivery ramp (550-600 in 2026, 650-750 mid-term) and the 20% p.a. Power Systems data-centre growth mature, reaching 2.5% by year 10. Margin held essentially flat - no credit for expansion beyond guidance because the H1 FY2026 22.5% margin carried LTSA contract catch-ups. Working capital captures 15% of each year's revenue increase (net LTSA balance growth GBP0.6bn in 2025 on GBP2.3bn revenue growth, 26%, haircut for the guided GBP150-200m supply-chain cash cost and lower 2026 LTSA growth); it shrinks automatically as growth slows. Cash tax ramps 22% -> 25% (TTM cash tax ~20% of underlying PBT; UK statutory 25%, H1 2026 flagged 'higher cash tax'). Capex 4.8% fading to 4.4% against D&A rising to 3.3% (Indianapolis, Istanbul MRO, UltraFan, Series 4000).

bull.narrative: Guidance keeps being beaten: Civil Aerospace operating margin pushes past 27% as time-on-wing doubles and LTSA margins keep expanding, Power Systems compounds data-centre back-up power at the targeted ~20% p.a. with a 20%+ margin, and Defence ramps on EJ200 exports, AUKUS, GCAP and F130. Group EBITDA margin reaches 28.5% (operating margin ~23.5%) by year 5 and holds; revenue growth 14% then 11/9/8/7%. LTSA balance growth captures 20% of revenue growth. Terminal cap 20x (GE Aerospace / Safran-style compounder multiple). SMR is still only in at carrying value - any commercial SMR fleet is upside to this case.

bear.narrative: The H1 2026 guidance lands (year-1 growth 8%, margin 24%) but the cycle turns in 2027-28: a widebody demand/airline-capex downturn (Middle East conflict, tariffs, recession) cuts OE deliveries and large-engine flying hours, and a new in-service durability problem (Trent XWB-97 / Trent 1000 history) brings remediation cost and capex at 5.5% of revenue. Revenue falls 2% in year 3 and is flat in year 4; EBITDA margin compresses to 19.5-20% (operating margin ~14-15%, i.e. the FY2024 level of 13.8% plus a little self-help) and stays there. The LTSA balance stops growing and shop-visit catch-up turns working capital into a 5% drag on revenue growth. Terminal cap 15x for a cyclical. Net cash means this is a value, not a solvency, case.

scenario_narratives.base: Rolls-Royce delivers FY2026 guidance (GBP4.7-4.9bn underlying operating profit, GBP3.8-4.0bn FCF) and converts the 2028 mid-term targets (GBP4.9-5.2bn, 18-20% margin, GBP5.0-5.3bn FCF) a year or two early as it has every target since 2023, but margins then plateau around 20-21% operating / 25% EBITDA: the aftermarket annuity on a 38% widebody installed-base share keeps growing with flying hours, Power Systems rides the data-centre cycle, Defence grows with NATO budgets, and growth fades from 11% to 2.5% over ten years as the OE delivery ramp matures. The LTSA cash tailwind shrinks with growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: A GE-Aerospace-style re-rating of the earnings base: time-on-wing and LTSA-margin gains lift Civil Aerospace above 27% margin, Power Systems compounds data-centre power at 20% p.a., Defence export and AUKUS/GCAP programmes ramp, and group EBITDA margin reaches 28.5% while revenue grows 14/11/9/8/7%. Buyback-funded flat share count, 20x terminal cap. SMR fleet economics are not in the numbers.
scenario_narratives.bear: Execution and cycle risk materialise together after the 2026 guidance year: widebody demand and flying hours roll over, a durability issue forces remediation spend, LTSA contract catch-ups unwind and the LTSA balance stops growing, so operating margin falls back to the FY2024 ~14% level and stays there with revenue flat for two years. Net cash and the A-/A3 rating keep it a value case rather than a solvency case; the 15x cap reflects a cyclical multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: Civil Aerospace OE and flying hours are genuinely cyclical, the FY2026 margin carries LTSA contract catch-ups that management itself flags, net LTSA balance growth is a customer-prepayment liability that reverses as shop visits catch up, and the company has a track record of in-service durability failures. Bull down to 25%: the bull case needs three independent things to hold at once (Civil margin >27%, Power Systems 20% p.a. for five years, Defence ramp) and the current price already discounts most of it. No live corporate action.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the transformed Rolls-Royce on the owner cash it will throw off from the FY2026 guided run-rate, with SBC, interest income and the full lease cash charged once and the share count held flat; take guidance as the base, not the H1 2026 peak margin, and charge the cycle in the bear scenario rather than in the discount rate. The question the price asks is not whether the turnaround is real - it is - but what return a buyer at ~1,385p is accepting for it; the required_return_table answers that directly.
key_risks_to_valuation: Peak-margin risk: FY2026 operating margin (~20%) includes LTSA contract catch-ups; the base holds it flat and the bear fades it to ~14-15% (FY2024 level)
LTSA balance growth is a customer-prepayment liability: the 15% working-capital capture shrinks with growth in the base and reverses in the bear
Widebody OE/flying-hour cyclicality and airline capex (Middle East conflict, tariffs, fuel) - the only operating segment with real downturn exposure is 52% of revenue
Engine durability / new-programme execution (Trent XWB-97, UltraFan, Series 4000, SMR licensing) - history of multi-year remediation costs

Discount rate: the valuation is terminal-heavy (Gordon at 9% / 2.5% implies ~15.8x year-10 FCF); the market price implies a required return around 7%, so the gap to IV is largely a cost-of-capital disagreement, not a cash-flow one
Bridge generosity: all GBP6.5bn cash counted as surplus although part backs GBP17bn of LTSA contract liabilities; SMR added at carrying value with its losses left in the flows (offsetting direction)
Legacy hedge book: GBP148m/yr excess-derivative settlements kept in the flows (company excludes them from its FCF); winding down
